data.narrative:
Antora Energy is a Series C-stage thermal energy storage company in the Climate & Energy sector. The valuation assessment draws on a universe of 3 same-stage, same-sector private peers (KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy) and incorporates broader Climate & Energy comps including public reference Ørsted (LNZA) and later-stage private companies like Helion and Redwood Materials.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis applied a 1.7x step-up multiplier to Antora's $550M total raised proxy, yielding $935M. Peer-median analysis across the 3 same-stage, same-sector comparables produced a median valuation of $1.0B, with individual peer valuations ranging from $700M (Amogy) to $3.0B (KoBold Metals). The wide peer range reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity and capital intensity within the thermal storage subsector.

Triangulation of both methods supports a valuation range of $795M to $1.1B, with a median point estimate of $968M. The 38% spread between low and high reflects material uncertainty around market penetration risk and relative technology positioning versus peers. KoBold Metals' $3.0B valuation sits notably above the peer median, suggesting valuation dispersion driven by stage variance and perceived capital requirements rather than sector-wide consensus. The binding constraint on upside is clarity on commercial deployment timelines and competitive differentiation relative to the peer set.
